name: Possession 4-1-4-1

slots.why: Sweeper keeper is the extra passer in build-up and covers the space behind a higher line.
Support full-back offers a wide passing option.
Ball-playing defender starts moves with passes into midfield.
Central defender who defends while his partner plays. Cover is the alternate.
Deep-lying playmaker is the base of the team, receiving from the defence and distributing it.
Wide midfielder (Support) is the safer flank, keeping the shape and passing inside.
Supporting central midfielder provides a short passing option and links play.
Box-to-box midfielder supplies runs from deep so the possession has a target.

Winger (Attack) supplies width and forward runs on the right, giving the dropping striker an outlet and joining the BBM as an attacking runner. The left wide midfielder remains on Support to preserve a safer passing flank.

Deep-Lying Forward (Support) drops to link possession and release the attacking right winger or arriving BBM. Complete Forward (Support) is an alternative for a striker with the broader technical and physical profile to link and finish.

description: A patient possession structure with a playmaker at the base, a linking striker and an attacking right winger who turns controlled build-up into a goal threat.
whyGood: The deep playmaker and supporting midfielders keep passing distances short, while the DLF can release the right winger and arriving BBM. The safer left flank balances that forward movement.
whyThisShape: A 4-1-4-1 built around patient possession: a deep-lying playmaker sits in front of the defence and a sweeper keeper joins the build-up. The CM(S) and left WM(S) provide short passing options, while the BBM and right W(A) make forward runs for the DLF(S) to find. Lower Tempo and Hold Shape keep clean regains connected to that structure before an opening is exploited. The team aims to control the game while retaining an attacking outlet.
whenToUse: When your squad is technically better than the opponent's and you want patient control with a linking striker and a right winger capable of turning possession into chances.
whenNotToUse: When you need immediate, high-tempo attacks, your defenders and midfield are uncomfortable on the ball, or the right winger lacks the movement to support the dropping striker. The attacking winger also makes this a less conservative choice for protecting a narrow lead.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Lower Tempo: Allow the passing structure to form during settled possession; a selected Counter instruction still applies immediately after regains.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Hold Shape: Retain the available passing structure after a regain rather than forcing an immediate counter.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

keyRequirements: An attacking right winger with the movement and pace to give the linking striker a forward outlet
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
